name: 'Ashiq Pasha
bio: Gibb calls 'Ashiq Pasha the earliest writer of the Ottomans, who flourished in the reign of Orkhan and lived in the town of Qir-Shehr in Anatolia; his title Pasha is a spiritual one, as he was a chief among mystics rather than a leader of warriors.
The poems here are taken from E. J. W. Gibb's Ottoman Poems (1882), the first English verse translations of Ottoman poetry; dates and biographical details follow Gibb's Biographical Notices.

poems.title: All the Universe
poems.author: 'Ashiq Pasha
poems.text:
All the Universe, one mighty sign, is shown;
God hath myriads of creative acts unknown:

None hath seen them, of the races jinn and men,
None hath news brought from that realm far off from ken.

Never shall thy mind or reason reach that strand,
Nor can tongue the King's name utter of that land.

Since 'tis His each nothingness with life to vest,
Trouble is there ne'er at all to His behest.

Eighteen thousand worlds, from end to end,
Do not with Him one atom's worth transcend.
